facts.title: The Patmahayr
facts.text: Known as the "father of Armenian history", Moses of Chorene wrote the first continuous history of his nation.

facts.title: Around 410
facts.text: Born around 410, he studied under Mesrop Mashtots and learned Greek, Syriac, and Pahlavi.

facts.title: Alexandria
facts.text: Sent to Alexandria, he studied rhetoric, grammar, and philosophy before returning to Armenia.

facts.title: History of Armenia
facts.text: Commissioned by Sahak Bagratuni, his major work traces from the biblical origins of Hayk to the 5th century.

facts.title: The Gusans
facts.text: By listening to pagan minstrels, he preserved unique legends such as the song of the birth of Vahagn.

facts.title: The City of Van
facts.text: His accounts of Van and its cuneiform inscriptions led to the rediscovery of the Urartian language.
In 1993, Armenia established the prestigious Movses Khorenatsi Medal to honor figures in culture.

ytTitle: Moses of Chorene: The Founding Father of Armenian History
ytLead: A disciple of Mesrop Mashtots in the 5th century, Moses of Chorene composed the first great historical chronicle of his nation. His History of Armenia immortalized the myths, kings, and memory of the Armenian people.
